name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat but Democratic nominee Gilbert heavily outraises and outspends the Republican
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95%
No general-election polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The district's D+22 lean, the Democrat's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win around 95% all point to a comfortable hold despite Frederica Wilson's retirement. With no polling available, uncertainty stays elevated but the fundamentals leave little doubt about the likely winner.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or a divided Democratic primary aftermath could narrow the margin, though a Republican win remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Frederica Wilson's retirement opens this heavily Democratic Miami-area seat, but the district's D+22 partisan lean makes it very difficult terrain for Republicans. Democrat Oliver Gilbert has raised more than $800,000 and benefits from substantial outside support, while Republican Te Mayonna Brown has raised about $313,000 with no reported outside spending.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no general-election polls, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which strongly favor Democrats holding the seat comfortably.
